clue.text: 19 born on part of mountain?

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for born, as in genealogies
a ridge is the long crest that forms part of a mountain

explanation.surface: Someone born high up on a mountain spur.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is COMPOSER, the theme answer: Frank Bridge was an English composer and Britten's teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Bridge was an English composer of chamber and orchestral music.

clue.text: Upset plump one coming in bearing almond biscuit

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the whole build reads backwards
coming in means the pieces enter the bearing word

parts.note: air means bearing, manner, as in 'an air of confidence'
fat means plump
a means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: A plump person tips over a tray of almond biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' puts the plump word and A inside the bearing word; 'Upset' turns the whole build over, as a down clue reads bottom to top. 'bearing' looks like a compass direction but means manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratafia is a small macaroon flavoured with almonds or almond essence.

clue.text: Boat going under Dee in the night

indicators.note: in a down clue, going under places this piece below the one before

parts.note: dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
an ark is a boat, like Noah's

explanation.surface: A boat sailing on the River Dee at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dee' is the name of the letter D, though it looks like the Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark is the time after nightfall, as in 'home before dark'.

clue.text: Warehouse, smart in style, getting set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised upside down, so the whole build reads backwards
in means the smart word goes inside the style word

parts.note: tone means style, character
pert means smart, jaunty

explanation.surface: A fashionable warehouse being built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' nests smart inside style, and 'getting set up' turns the whole build over, as a down clue reads bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepot is a trading depot where goods are stored for re-export.

clue.text: 19's a nobleman? Right

parts.note: Bart is the abbreviation for baronet, a hereditary titled rank
OK means all right, correct

explanation.surface: Asking whether a musician is a titled aristocrat, then agreeing.
explanation.walkthrough: '19's' reads as 'the composer is': Bela Bartok was the Hungarian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bela Bartok was a twentieth-century Hungarian composer and pianist.

clue.text: Daughter is turning up in gathering next door?

indicators.note: in means the turned pieces go inside the gathering word

parts.note: a bee is a social gathering, as in a sewing bee

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the pieces read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A daughter appears at a neighbours' party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes SID from D and IS, and 'in' sets it into BEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside means at the side of, close by, as a neighbour is.

clue.text: Take a speed charge — as a result of this?

definitions.text: Take a speed charge — as a result of this?

parts.words: Take a speed charge — as a result of this?
parts.note: reads as a motorist fined for speeding after being caught by the police device that measures speed

explanation.surface: A driver fined for speeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A radar trap is a police speed check that catches drivers going too fast.

clue.text: Describing sight: A sudden movement amidst stone'

indicators.note: amidst means the other pieces go in the middle of the stone word

parts.note: an opal is a gemstone
a tic is an involuntary sudden twitch

explanation.surface: A twitch catches the eye among gemstones.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says 'A sudden movement', but the twitch comes before the A in the answer; 'amidst' puts both inside the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to vision or the eyes.

clue.text: Saturday and priest's without an opening — gets sodden with drink!

indicators.note: losing the opening letter means the first letter of the priest word is dropped

parts.note: a curate is a junior priest; with the possessive 's it gives the letters of 'curate's'

explanation.surface: A weekend bender with the vicar's assistant ends in a drunken soaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without an opening' drops the first letter of the priest's title. Saturate is transitive, so the definition reads as 'makes sodden', a loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To saturate is to soak something until it can absorb no more liquid.

clue.text: 19 varied tunes — a shock

indicators.note: varied means changed about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer's changing melodies give the audience a jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' rearranges TUNES A SHOCK. Karlheinz Stockhausen's electronic music did shock audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Karlheinz Stockhausen was a German composer of electronic and avant-garde music.

clue.text: Fruit consumed in environs of Damascus

indicators.note: the eating word is placed inside the frame taken from the city's name
the environs of a word are its outskirts, its first and last letters

parts.note: consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Fruit eaten on the outskirts of the Syrian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of Damascus, D and S, go round ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dates are the sweet fruit of the date palm, grown widely in the Middle East.

clue.text: Society attitudes about that place may be in tatters

indicators.note: about means the attitudes word goes around the place word

parts.note: miens are bearings or attitudes
there means in that place

explanation.surface: Social attitudes there may end up ripped to shreds.
explanation.walkthrough: The attitudes word is split by the place word; 'may be in' links to tatters, since things are torn 'to smithereens' or 'into tatters'.
explanation.definitionFit: Smithereens are small fragments, as tatters are torn shreds.

clue.text: 19's otherwise very loud

parts.note: or means otherwise, as in 'hurry or you'll miss it'
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A remark that a composer is, alternatively, extremely loud.
explanation.walkthrough: '19's' reads as 'the composer is': Carl Orff wrote Carmina Burana.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff was the German composer best known for Carmina Burana.

clue.text: 19 arranged keen price, without minimum of doubt?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the reworked letters sit around the small piece
arranged means put into a new order, so these letters are reshuffled
the minimum of a word is its smallest part, here its first letter

explanation.surface: A buyer arranging a sharp price with hardly any hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' reshuffles KEEN PRICE; 'without' (outside) puts those letters round D, the first letter of doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Krzysztof Penderecki was a Polish composer of avant-garde and choral works.

clue.text: Sound of firework closed -a Volcano?

indicators.note: the sound of the phrase means it is said aloud to give the answer

parts.note: a cracker is a small exploding firework; to means closed, as of a door pushed to; the indefinite article, A

explanation.surface: Fireworks go quiet beside an erupting mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, CRACKER TO A runs together into the name of the Indonesian volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Krakatoa is the Indonesian volcanic island whose 1883 eruption was heard thousands of miles away.

clue.text: Tune's initially rejected amongst group of players? It's a blow

parts.note: an air is a tune; with the 's it gives airs

indicators.note: amongst means the letter goes inside the players word

parts.note: a team is a group of players

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A team discard a tune and find it a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a blow' sounds like a setback, but means a current of air.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstream is a current of moving air, something that blows.

clue.text: Chap's abbreviated description of sacred river

indicators.note: abbreviated means shortened to its initial, as in the map abbreviation R for river

parts.note: Alph is the sacred river of Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan

explanation.surface: A man's name cut down from a description of a holy river.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's Kubla Khan has 'Alph, the sacred river', so the sacred river abbreviated is R. Alph, read as a man's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is a common male first name, and a chap is a man.

clue.text: 19 handy in love, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A handy composer falls in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges HANDY IN with O. Erno Dohnanyi was the Hungarian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erno Dohnanyi was a Hungarian composer, pianist and conductor.

clue.text: 19's a poor painter — no end of bad

indicators.note: no here means the following piece is removed from the painter word

parts.note: a dauber is an unskilled painter who daubs

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Calling a composer an inept artist, with nothing bad at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the last letter of bad, comes off DAUBER. Daniel Auber was the French opera composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Auber was a nineteenth-century French composer of comic operas.

clue.text: 19's own country, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are said aloud

parts.note: Britain is the composer's own country

explanation.surface: Naming a composer's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: BRITAIN said aloud gives BRITTEN. '19's' reads as 'the composer's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten was the English composer of Peter Grimes.

clue.text: One's noted first three in competition puzzle

indicators.note: the first three letters of the word that follows are taken

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling question

explanation.surface: A competitor reaching the top three in a puzzle contest.
explanation.walkthrough: COM is the first three letters of competition. The definition plays on 'noted': a composer is one who puts down musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes music, setting it down in written notes.

clue.text: 19, second one held in support

indicators.note: held in means the single letter goes inside the support word

parts.note: a truss is a supporting frame or bandage
a means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: A composer's backing performer is propped up.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside TRUSS, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Strauss and Richard Strauss were both composers, the first of waltzes, the second of operas.

clue.text: 19 getting support before the Spanish

indicators.note: before means the support word comes ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a hand is help or support, as in 'give a hand'
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A composer getting backing ahead of a Spanish tour.
explanation.walkthrough: George Frideric Handel wrote Messiah.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was the German-born composer of Messiah.

clue.text: 19 broadcast nastiness about American

indicators.note: about means the reshuffled letters are placed around the abbreviation
broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Radio programmes spreading spite about the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges NASTINESS, and 'about' puts it round A. Camille Saint-Saens was the French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Camille Saint-Saens was the French composer of The Carnival of the Animals.

clue.text: 19 filling clear need?

indicators.note: filling means the answer sits inside the run of words, across their join

explanation.surface: A composer satisfying an obvious demand.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'cleAR NEed'. Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne was an eighteenth-century English composer of Rule, Britannia!

clue.text: Man, say, is only half male

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, here its second half

explanation.surface: A man is only half masculine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea; 'say' marks it as an example. LE is the second half of male.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island.

clue.text: Partially inverting

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Partially inverting (5)' has no definition: the answer is reversed hidden in 'inverting', so 'inverting' would be both the reversal indicator and the fodder; no scan or reprint gives the missing words.

clue.text: Sad ruins collapsing round old fossils?

indicators.note: round means the reshuffled letters go around the single letter
collapsing means falling apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy picture of crumbling ancient ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' rearranges SAD RUINS, and 'round' puts it round O. The question mark marks old fogeys called fossils, or creatures known from fossils.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinosaurs are extinct reptiles known from fossil remains, and the word also means old-fashioned people.

clue.text: Creature I'm involving in analysis? Not half

indicators.note: involving in means the short piece is set inside the other one
only half the word is kept, its first four letters

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A creature being examined, though the study is only half done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' keeps the first half of analysis, and 'involving in' sets I'M inside that half.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is any living creature, as opposed to a plant.

clue.text: Bridge ploy with no little force intrinsically

indicators.note: with no means the following piece is taken away from the card play

parts.note: a finesse is a card-playing tactic in bridge to win a trick with a lower card
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: A card trick played without any real strength.
explanation.walkthrough: IN ESSE is Latin for 'in actual being', the opposite of in posse.
explanation.definitionFit: In esse means in actual existence, belonging to a thing's own essential nature.
